# Lab 2.10: Primary & Foreign Keys

## What We Are Going to Do
Add unenforced primary and foreign keys, and see the optimiser use them to skip a join.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create a small star schema.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab02.dim_users AS
SELECT id AS user_id, first_name, country
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users`;

CREATE TABLE lab02.fact_orders AS
SELECT order_id, user_id, status, num_of_item
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Add the keys.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">ALTER TABLE lab02.dim_users ADD PRIMARY KEY (user_id) NOT ENFORCED;
ALTER TABLE lab02.fact_orders ADD PRIMARY KEY (order_id) NOT ENFORCED;
ALTER TABLE lab02.fact_orders
  ADD CONSTRAINT fk_user FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES lab02.dim_users(user_id) NOT ENFORCED;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Run a join that only needs the fact table.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT f.status, SUM(f.num_of_item) AS items
FROM lab02.fact_orders f
INNER JOIN lab02.dim_users d ON f.user_id = d.user_id
GROUP BY f.status;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Open **Execution graph**. `dim_users` is not read, because the keys prove every order has exactly one user. This is **join elimination**.

4. **[CLI] View the constraints.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq show --format=prettyjson lab02.fact_orders | grep -A15 tableConstraints
bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT * FROM lab02.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLE_CONSTRAINTS'</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Remember the risk.** BigQuery does not check the keys. If you insert duplicate `user_id` values into `dim_users`, queries can return wrong results.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Keys | Metadata only, `NOT ENFORCED` |
| Join elimination | `dim_users` skipped in the plan |
| Constraints | Listed in TABLE_CONSTRAINTS |
| Responsibility | You keep the keys true |
